IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 336 of 2015
with
CLMA No. 8007 of 2015 (Delay Condonation Application)
Pratap Singh Bisht. ……..Appellant 
 Versus 
State of Uttarakhand & others. …….Respondents 
 
Mr. M.C. Kandpal, Senior Advocate, assisted by Mr. Chitrarth Kandpal, Advocate for 
the appellant. 
Mr. J.C. Pandey, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand. 
Mr. Anil Kumar Joshi, Advocate for respondent no. 6. 
Dated: 11th December, 2017
Coram: Hon’ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon’ble V.K. Bist, J.
K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral)
 There is delay of 101 days in filing the 
Appeal. 
2. In the circumstances, the application for 
condonation of delay is allowed and the delay in filing 
the Appeal stands condoned. 
3. Appellant is the writ petitioner. Appellant 
sought to quash the order dated 30.10.2012 passed by 
the sixth respondent, who is the Principal of an aided 
Inter College. Further direction was sought to appoint 
the appellant on the post of Class-IV in the said 
institution on the basis of Dying-in-Harness Rules. 
4. The case of the appellant, in brief, is as 
follows: 
2017:UHC:10448 2
 The appellant’s father was a Class-IV 
employee in the institution of the sixth respondent and 
he expired in the childhood of the appellant. The sixth 
respondent is a minority institution, which is receiving 
aid. Appellant’s mother was appointed in the 
institution on the post of Mali on the basis of Dying-in￾Harness Rules. The mother of the appellant also died 
on 24.01.2007, leaving behind appellant as her legal 
heir. By Annexure No. 2, on the basis of application of 
the appellant, the Principal sent a letter to the District 
Education Officer, Almora on 28.02.2007 to appoint 
the appellant on the Class-IV post on the basis of the 
Dying-in-Harness Rules, as the mother of the appellant 
expired on 24.01.2007. It is further submitted that the 
Principal, Teachers, Employees working in the class III 
& IV posts are getting the salary from the government 
exchequer. There is reference to notification dated 
02.02.1995, as per which, the provision of the 
appointment on Dying-in-Harness Rules is applicable
to all aided schools and was affirmed by the 
notification dated 09.08.2001. Further case of the
appellant is that when he was not appointed, he filed 
an application before the District Education Officer. 
Three posts of class IV were vacant in the institution 
and the Principal has asked for permission to advertise 
the three posts of class-IV, which were vacant in the 
institution. An advertisement was issued. The 
Principal/Public Information Officer, Adam Girls Inter 
College, Almora, vide letter dated 16.02.2010, informed 
the appellant that he may file an application for 
appointment on the basis of the Dying-in-Harness 
2017:UHC:10448 3
Rules, while the appellant has already made an 
application on 31.08.2007. The Director School 
Education has, by Annexure No.3 letter dated 
30.06.2011, stated that Dying-in-Harness is also 
applicable to the minority institutions. Appellant filed 
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1065 of 2011. This Court 
disposed of the writ petition directing the respondent 
no. 5 to consider the representation of the appellant. 
Appellant filed another representation Annexure No.5. 
By the impugned order, the case of the appellant was 
rejected. Pleadings were exchanged and the writ 
petition was dismissed. In doing so, the learned Single 
Judge took note of the stand of the sixth respondent 
that there is no provision for compassionate 
appointment in the minority grant-in-aid school. It is 
stated that, in Regulation 103 made under the U.P. 
Intermediate Education Act, 1921, Dying-in-Harness is 
not applicable to the minority grant-in-aid school. 
Secondly, it is the case of the respondents that the 
appellant was not found suitable. Further, the Court 
found as follows: 
“3. After creation of the State of 
Uttarakhand on 09.11.2000, the 
regulations, known as “Uttarakhand 
School Education Regulations, 2009”, 
have been framed under the 
Uttarakhand School Education Act, 
2006. Under Regulation 91, such 
appointment can be made in a grant-in￾aid school. Even under Regulation 91 
there is no provision that such 
appointment can be given in a grant-in￾aid minority school but even assuming 
that under the regulations framed in the 
2017:UHC:10448 4
year 2009 such appointment can be 
made, the regulations became applicable 
in the year 2011 whereas mother of the 
petitioner expired in the year 2007. 
Therefore, there is no provision for 
appointment on compassionate ground 
in a grant-in-aid minority institute. 
4. The case of the petitioner further is 
that such appointment has been given 
not only in the case of the father and 
mother of the petitioner but in other 
cases as well. This may be so, but merely 
because such appointment has been 
given to the father and mother of the 
petitioner, he cannot claim appointment 
on compassionate ground as a matter of 
right, since there is no provision of law 
presently enforced in the minority grant￾in-aid school under which such an 
appointment can be granted. 
5. In view thereof, no direction can be 
given to the school to make such an 
appointment. Further the respondents 
have also stated in the impugned order 
that the petitioner was called for 
interview, along with other persons, for 
the post of Peon, in which petitioner was 
not found suitable. Hence, such an 
appointment cannot be given to the 
petitioner. Further, there is also no other 
vacant post in the school on which such 
an appointment can be made.” 
5. Finding that no direction can be given to the 
respondent to make such an appointment on 
compassionate ground, the writ petition was dismissed. 
6. We heard Mr. M.C. Kandpal, learned Senior 
Counsel, assisted by Mr. Chitrarth Kandpal, learned
counsel for the appellant, Mr. Anil Kumar Joshi, 
2017:UHC:10448 5
learned counsel appearing for the respondent no. 6 and 
also Mr. J.C. Pandey, learned Brief Holder for the State 
of Uttarakhand. 
7. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the 
appellant would refer us to a judgment of the Division 
Bench of Allahabad High Court in the matter of 
Committee of Management, National Inter College and
others Vs. State of U.P. and others, reported in (2012) 
6 ADJ 741. He would point out that, in that case also, 
the respondent employee died in the year 1998, yet the 
authorities had granted the benefit of Dying-in￾Harness. 
8. Per contra, learned Brief Holder for the State 
would submit that the relevant provision, which is 
applicable, is the provision contained in Regulation 
103, which proviso was applicable in the State of 
Uttarakhand, as on the date of the death of the mother 
of the appellant and, as per the same, appellant is not 
entitled. 
9. Mr. Anil Kumar Joshi, learned counsel for 
the sixth respondent would reiterate the stand that, 
under Regulation 103, the law which was applicable in 
the State of U.P. on the appointed day, the proviso did 
not extend the benefit of Dying-In-Harness to minority 
aided institutions. He would submit that the 
amendment, which took place in the State of U.P., was 
in the year 2001, by which the proviso to Regulation 
2017:UHC:10448 6
103 was repealed; but, this will not assist the 
appellant. 
10. It is not in dispute that, under the U.P. 
Education Act, 2006, Regulations have been framed in 
the year 2009. Under Regulation 91 thereof, the Right 
to Compassionate Appointment is given and there is no 
exemption in favour of the minority institutions in
Regulation 91. 
11. As far as judgment of the Allahabad High 
Court is concerned, we cannot agree with it if it is 
understood as laying down that in respect of the death 
which took place in the year 1998, the provision of
Dying-in-Harness, which was not applicable as on the 
date of the death; but, which became applicable 
consequent on the repeal of the proviso in the year
2001 would still be available to an employee. A 
compassionate appointment cannot be claimed as a 
right. Compassionate appointment is made available
either on the basis of the Scheme or a Statute or an 
Order. In the absence of the same, no employee can
claim a right to be appointed by way of compassionate 
appointment. It may be another matter that the 
institution may have made such appointments, as 
found by the learned Single Judge and complained of
by the learned Senior Counsel for the appellant; but, 
again we agree with the learned Single Judge that it 
may not give a legal right to seek a mandamus or have 
the order quashed. 
2017:UHC:10448 7
12. In short, we may sum up the legal position. 
By way of Regulation inserted in the year 1995, in 
Regulation 103, it provided for appointment by Dying￾in-Harness for employees like the appellant. However, 
it contained the proviso, which rendered it inapplicable 
to minority institutions. The State of Uttarakhand was 
born on 09.11.2000. Therefore, the law contained in 
Regulation 103 became applicable. It was the law, 
which was applicable in the year 2007, when the 
appellant’s mother died. Under the said law, the 
appellant could not possibly claim as a matter of legal 
right the benefit of appointment in Dying-in-Harness in 
the sixth respondent institution being a minority 
institution though receiving aid. The amendment in
the year 2001 in the State of U.P. by which the proviso 
to Regulation 103 was deleted cannot have any effect 
on the legal rights of the parties involved in this case. 
The subsequent enactment of the Regulation under the 
Uttarakhand Education Act in the year 2009 also, 
though it may create a right prospectively, cannot 
advance the case of the appellant as it does not has 
retrospective operation. Therefore, in the absence of 
any legal right given by any law or order or scheme, the 
appellant cannot claim a right to be appointed under 
the Dying-in-Harness Scheme. 
13. Obviously, the letter which was written by 
the Government stating that in the year 2011 the 
Dying-in-Harness was applicable to the minority 
institution also is apparently based on the Regulations 
of 2009. Equally, the fact that the sixth respondent 
2017:UHC:10448 8
has sent a letter for appointment of the appellant 
under the Dying-in-Harness Scheme may not by itself
give a legal right to the appellant to claim benefit of 
Dying-in-Harness Scheme when the matter is 
considered in the Court. Then, lastly, there is a case of 
Mr. A.K. Joshi, learned counsel appearing for the sixth 
respondent that appellant was considered in the 
interview and he was not found suitable; but, that was 
alongwith all others; but, we need not go into the said 
matter in view of the absence of the legal right. 
14. Accordingly, the Appeal fails and is 
dismissed. 
15. There will be no order as to costs. 
(V.K. Bist, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.) 
11.12.2017
Arpan
